page.title: Release readiness
page.purpose: Walk the owner from no account to a production listing, naming at every rung what is done, what is blocked, and what only a person can do.

priorities.statement: Rungs are ordered, and a later rung never reports ready while an earlier one is not.
priorities.notes: Order is the information. A ladder whose rungs can be read independently is just a checklist.

priorities.statement: Each rung states plainly whether the ramp can complete it or only the owner can.
priorities.notes: Registration, identity verification, and payment are irreducibly human. Implying otherwise wastes the owner's time.

priorities.statement: Each rung shows its cost where one exists.
priorities.notes: A $25 registration is a decision, not a task. The surface should not hide that it costs money.

priorities.statement: Dated obligations are shown with their dates.
priorities.notes: Target API 36 by 31 August 2026 and developer verification from 30 September 2026 are deadlines, not preferences.

priorities.statement: Rung state is re-probed, never read from a stored flag.
priorities.notes: A lapsed or revoked account must not continue to read as satisfied.

states.description: No Play Console account exists. The first rung is the only actionable one and every later rung is explicitly blocked by it.
Registration is complete and developer verification is submitted but not granted. Distinguishes 'waiting on Google' from 'waiting on you'.
Every rung satisfied; the internal testing track is available.

claims.statement: No rung reports ready while any rung it depends on is unsatisfied.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-009. A ladder that can report a later rung ready out of order is not modelling a dependency, it is displaying independent flags.

claims.statement: Every rung indicates whether it can be automated by the ramp or requires an owner action.
claims.rationale: The purpose of the surface is to tell the owner what to do next; conflating 'blocked on you' with 'blocked on the system' defeats it.

claims.statement: A rung awaiting a third-party decision is visually and textually distinct from a rung awaiting an owner action.
claims.rationale: Verification review can take days. An owner who cannot tell these apart will either wait on themselves or act on something already submitted.
